The submitted answer of 20 is the total kilograms at the reduced price, not the number of additional kilograms. The script below computes the extra quantity exactly.

```python
from fractions import Fraction as F

budget = F(1000)
new_price = F(50)
reduction = F(25, 100)

# Reduced price = original * (1 - reduction), so original = new / (1 - reduction)
old_price = new_price / (1 - reduction)

# Sanity check: the reduction really is 25%
assert new_price == old_price * (1 - reduction)

old_kg = budget / old_price
new_kg = budget / new_price
extra_kg = new_kg - old_kg

print("Original price per kg:", old_price, float(old_price))
print("Kg for Rs. 1000 before reduction:", old_kg)
print("Kg for Rs. 1000 after reduction:", new_kg)
print("Additional kg obtainable:", extra_kg)

claimed = F(20)
print("Submitted answer:", claimed)
print("CHECK PASS" if extra_kg == claimed else "CHECK FAIL")
```
